implemented: Preserved the existing Sprint 1 Travel Candidate Organizer MVP in build/ with the single-page planner, local candidate matching, sorting, statuses, notes, comparison view, regenerate flow, reset flow, and no-match guidance.
Updated build/package.json so npm run dev uses a Windows launcher that keeps the app targeted at http://localhost:3000 instead of silently drifting to another port when 3000 is already occupied.
Added build/scripts/dev.ps1 to detect an existing listener on port 3000, attempt to stop it before launching Next.js, and fail with a clear recovery message if Windows refuses the stop request.
Updated build/README.md to document the port-3000 launcher behavior and the manual recovery path when another app is still bound to that port.

npm run build is still blocked in this sandbox by Next.js worker-process startup restrictions (spawn EPERM), so validation here relied on TypeScript compile plus launcher behavior checks instead of a full production build.
